name: Gehazi
bio:
Gehazi was Elisha's servant. When Elisha wanted to reward a Shunammite woman who had built him a guest room, Gehazi pointed out that she had no son and her husband was old, prompting Elisha's promise that she would bear a son within the year (2 Kings 4:12-17). Years later, when that son died suddenly, Gehazi was sent ahead with Elisha's staff to lay on the child's face, but it produced no response — only Elisha's own prayer and physical contact with the boy brought him back to life (2 Kings 4:29-37).

## 📖 Core Story: The Leprosy of Naaman

After Elisha healed Naaman, commander of Syria's army, of leprosy and refused any payment for it, Gehazi decided privately that his master had let a reward go to waste. He chased Naaman down and lied, claiming Elisha now wanted a talent of silver and two changes of clothing for two visiting prophets; Naaman gladly gave double, sending it with two servants. Gehazi hid the goods and lied again to Elisha about where he'd been, but Elisha already knew — his heart had gone with Gehazi in spirit — and asked whether this was a time to accept money, garments, and property. For this, Elisha pronounced that Naaman's leprosy would cling to Gehazi and his descendants forever, and Gehazi left Elisha's presence "a leper as white as snow" (2 Kings 5:20-27).

## 📖 Core Story: Telling the King of Elisha's Deeds

Gehazi later appears recounting Elisha's great deeds to the king of Israel, and happened to be describing how Elisha had restored the Shunammite woman's dead son to life at the very moment she herself arrived to petition the king for her house and land — confirming her story and leading the king to order everything restored to her (2 Kings 8:1-6).
